top.headline: Air India Sets Up a Dedicated Cost-Savings Team and Tightens Spending Approvals, Its Chief Executive Tells Employees in a Memo
chunks: Air India has set up a dedicated team to identify cost savings across its operations and tightened spending approvals, Chief Executive Tewolde Gebremariam told employees in an internal memo, according to the report. The memo cited airspace disruptions, the Middle East conflict and high jet fuel costs, according to the report.

top.headline: Social Democrats Say They Will Join Prime Minister-Designate Luca Niculescu's Proposed Government, Which Is to Be Unveiled on Thursday Before a Confidence Vote
chunks: The Social Democrats (PSD), parliament's largest party, will have 11 ministers in the proposed government that Prime Minister-designate Luca Niculescu will unveil on Thursday before a parliamentary vote of confidence, PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu said late on Wednesday, according to the report. Technocrats will fill other ministerial posts, including finance, energy and foreign affairs, according to the report; other pro-European parties said they will back Niculescu, ensuring the 233 votes required to win the vote of confidence, according to the report. Niculescu, 55, will lead President Nicusor Dan's fourth attempt to install a government in the five months since the previous coalition cabinet collapsed, according to the report; the PSD said it will join on condition that a 2027 budget
plan be unveiled by December 1, with no further tax hikes, according to the report.

top.headline: Rand Trades at 16.5575 Against the Dollar at 0638 GMT on Thursday, About 0.3% Firmer Than Its Previous Close
chunks: The rand traded at 16.5575 against the dollar at 0638 GMT on Thursday, about 0.3% firmer than its previous close, according to the report. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was firmer in early deals, with the yield falling 6.5 basis points to 8.69%, according to the report. Investors are looking ahead to Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana's medium-term budget policy statement next week, according to the report.

top.headline: British Land Expects Underlying Profit of £166 Million for the Six Months Ended September 30, Up From £155 Million a Year Earlier
chunks: British Land said on Thursday that it expects underlying profit of £166 million for the six months ended September 30, up from £155 million a year earlier, with underlying earnings per share of 16.1 pence, according to the report. The company reported 12% like-for-like rental income growth for the first half, according to the report; its retail parks portfolio was 99% occupied, with leasing 9.6% ahead of previous passing rents, according to the report. British Land reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 expectation of underlying earnings per share of at least 30.5 pence, according to the report.

top.headline: Jupiter Fund Management Reports Third-Quarter Net Inflows of £700 Million and Assets Under Management of £75.9 Billion at September 30
chunks: Jupiter Fund Management reported net inflows of £700 million in the third quarter, compared with £300 million a year earlier, reversing second-quarter outflows of £800 million, according to the report. Assets under management rose 51% to £75.9 billion at September 30, compared with £50.4 billion a year earlier, according to the report. Retail, wholesale and investment trust net inflows reached £1.0 billion, a fifth consecutive quarter of positive flows in that channel, according to the report.

top.headline: Travis Perkins Reports a 1.3% Fall in Third-Quarter Like-for-Like Sales and a 1.6% Fall in Group Revenue
chunks: Travis Perkins reported a 1.3% fall in like-for-like sales in the third quarter and a 1.6% fall in third-quarter group revenue, according to the report. Chief Executive Gavin Slark said the company's cost discipline and trading approach are protecting profitability while it implements further operational efficiencies, according to the report.

top.headline: French Consumer Prices Rose 3.4% Year-on-Year in September on an EU-Harmonised Basis, INSEE Says
chunks: Consumer prices in France rose 3.4% year-on-year in September on an EU-harmonised basis, statistics office INSEE said on Thursday, in line with a preliminary reading from late September, according to the report. The harmonised rate accelerated from 2.6% in August and was at its highest level since January 2024, according to the report.

top.headline: Vatican Says Pope Leo Had a Good Night in Hospital and Has Eaten Breakfast; His Public Schedule Is Canceled Until October 20
chunks: Pope Leo, recovering from surgery for lung cancer, had a good night in hospital and has eaten breakfast, the Vatican said on Thursday, according to the report. Leo, 71, was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung in surgery on Tuesday afternoon; the Vatican has said the surgery was completed successfully, without complications, and has not yet disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, according to the report. Further updates are expected on Thursday, the pathology report may not be available for several days, and Leo's public schedule has been canceled until October 20, according to the report.

top.headline: EasyJet Publishes the Scheme Document for Its £5.7 Billion Takeover by Apollo, With a Shareholder Vote Set for November
chunks: EasyJet on Thursday published the scheme document for its £5.7 billion takeover by Apollo, setting a shareholder vote for November, according to the report. The company reaffirmed its expectation to close the deal before the end of the first quarter of 2027, according to the report.

top.headline: Dunelm Reports Total Sales Up 1.1% to £433 Million in the 13 Weeks Ended September 26
chunks: Dunelm posted total sales up 1.1% to £433 million in the 13-week period ended September 26, according to the report. Digital sales rose 1% and accounted for 41% of total sales, according to the report; the company affirmed its annual profit expectations and said first-half profit will fall below prior-year levels, according to the report.
